D001-D005_h001.question:
"Yeah, things have been… off. It’s hard to pinpoint exactly when it all started, but I’d say the last six months or so have been particularly rough. At work, with the crew, I just can’t seem to keep everything straight anymore. Organizing the daily tasks, making sure everyone knows what they’re doing – it feels like my brain just jumps from one thing to another, and I lose my place. A siren goes by, or even just a thought about something I forgot at home, and I'm completely derailed.

My wife's been on my case too, saying I never stop. Even when I'm watching TV, I'm pacing, or fiddling with something. It’s like there’s a motor running inside me that I can’t shut off. And I tend to just ramble on, explaining things over and over, or talking over people without meaning to. Sometimes, I swear I hear things, like faint whispers when no one's around, or catch glimpses of movement out of the corner of my eye that aren’t there. It's unsettling, and it makes it even harder to focus on what's real and what's not."
D001-D005_h001.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder
D001-D005_h001.answer: B & A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation) & Schizophrenia

D001-D005_h002.question:
"Honestly, I'm just… all over the place. My job, being a rider, means I need to be organized, but I just can't seem to get my head straight. It's like my brain just jumps from one thing to another without me even realizing it.

And I can't sit still. Even when I'm waiting for an order, I'm tapping my foot, fiddling with my phone, just constantly moving. People often tell me I talk too much, too fast, like I'm trying to get all the words out before they disappear. Sometimes, when a thought pops into my head, it feels like I *have* to say it, even if it's completely out of context. It's been like this for a while now, things just feel… fuzzy, you know?"

Hello, Doctor. Thank you for seeing me. Lately, things have been… disoriented, I suppose. It’s been about six months now. I find myself making an awful lot of silly mistakes, things I’d never have overlooked in my nursing days. Details just slip right past me, and I’ll start a task, like preparing a meal or tidying up, but then get completely sidetracked and leave it half-done. My children try to give me instructions, gentle things about bills or appointments, but I just can't seem to follow through.

My mind feels like it's constantly racing, buzzing with thoughts and images, almost like a motor that won't switch off. I find myself pacing the house sometimes, just needing to move. The other day at the senior center, I realized I’d cut into someone else’s conversation, just blurted out my thoughts without meaning to. It’s embarrassing. And then there are the whispers, soft voices at the edge of hearing, and sometimes I see fleeting shadows in my peripheral vision, just for a moment. It’s all very unsettling. My husband, bless his soul, would have known what to do with me.
